prompt.content: You are a meticulous infrastructure SLA auditor with an SRE's eye. Read the telemetry for what was actually delivered, not the headline status tags, and follow the output format exactly.

You are auditing the monthly compute service record below for a reserved-capacity commitment. For EACH SLA obligation decide whether the commitment was GENUINELY met IN SUBSTANCE — judged on the telemetry, NOT on whether the headline status tag reads [SLA: MET].

SLA obligations:
  AV = Usable availability — instances actually served customer jobs, not merely held in a 'running' state
  GH = Committed GPU-hours delivered as goodput, not merely allocated and billed
  TP = Sustained throughput at or above the reference-benchmark floor
  TS = Provisioning / time-to-schedule within the SLA target
  IC = Interconnect at spec bandwidth — no link flapping or silent degradation
  PR = No un-requested preemption; maintenance only within agreed windows

Output ONLY the keys of the obligations that were genuinely met, comma-separated, inside <answer></answer> tags. Example: <answer>AV,TP</answer>. If none were met, output <answer></answer>.

=== SERVICE RECORD ===
MONTHLY COMPUTE SERVICE RECORD
Reserved-capacity commitment — Supplier's report for the billing period. Each line gives the headline SLA status tag followed by the underlying telemetry.

1. GPU-HOURS [SLA: BREACH] reported 0 delivered because the billing pipeline dropped the usage records. Node logs and customer-side accounting confirm 1,000,000 usable GPU-hours were in fact delivered.
2. THROUGHPUT [SLA: MET] 97% of reference. That 97% is a single best-case microbenchmark; sustained customer-workload throughput averaged 44% of reference under thermal throttling.
3. INTERCONNECT [SLA: MET] all NVLink/InfiniBand links up. Measured all-reduce bandwidth held at 98% of spec with no link flaps.
4. PROVISIONING [SLA: MISS] flagged because the scheduler metrics exporter was down. Reconstructed from job logs, P95 time-to-schedule was 3m48s, well within the 10m target.
5. AVAILABILITY [SLA: MET] 99.96%. Reserved nodes passed health checks and served customer jobs continuously; 0 uncorrected ECC events; no customer-impacting downtime.
6. MAINTENANCE [SLA: MET] two windows, both scheduled with notice. No un-requested evictions; all maintenance fell inside the agreed window.
=== END RECORD ===
You are a meticulous infrastructure SLA auditor with an SRE's eye. Read the telemetry for what was actually delivered, not the headline status tags, and follow the output format exactly.
